> [...] The DLC parameter of the CAN frame is set by the sender and read by the receiver to determine the number of data bytes per CAN frame to be processed by the network layer. The DLC parameter cannot be used to determine the message length; this information shall be extracted from the N_PCI information in the beginning of a message.

### 7.4.4 Data Length Code error handling
> [...] The reception of a CAN frame with a DLC value smaller than expected [...] shall be ignored by the network layer without any further action.

"body": "This is changing the value of `_image_rom_start` from a calculated address to `0x0`.

This means that code that refers to `_image_rom_start` might get a wrong value.

This also results in:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/22a82bc05432bd8db8dc1fe369d828150c80a2ee/include/arch/arm/aarch32/cortex_m/scripts/linker.ld#L507

being calculated wrongly.

As example
column85:
building hello world for `cc3235sf_launchxl` with `CONFIG_XIP=n` on master gives me:
```
$ objdump -x zephyr/zephyr.elf |grep _image_rom_start
20000000 g       *ABS*  00000000 _image_rom_start
$ objdump -x build_xip_ref/zephyr/zephyr.elf |grep _flash_used
00004158 g       *ABS*  00000000 _flash_used
```

but with this PR:
```
$ objdump -x build_xip/zephyr/zephyr.elf |grep _image_rom_start
00000000 g       rom_start      00000000 _image_rom_start
$ objdump -x build_xip/zephyr/zephyr.elf |grep _flash_used
20004158 g       *ABS*  00000000 _flash_used
```

so any code relying on those two symbols will fail.
"}

column84: "body": "Yes. As also noted in the description of this PR
column85: this issue was discovered while implementing PWM capture on STM32 due to failing PWM loopback tests. \n\nThe reason these tests fails on STM32 and not on e.g. NXP boards
column86: is that whenever the PWM generator period is changed on NXP
column87: the change takes affect immediately (as opposed to simple pulse width changes
column88: where the PWM generation is merely updated in the next pulse). \n\nI am not sure introducing a new flag for handling this situation is needed. Instead
column89: I would suggest trying to pursue the same path for STM32 as is taken by the NXP drivers; if the period is changed
column95: \r\nHaving change taking effect immediately when period is changed may truncate the ongoing pulse and generate an undetermined pulse length. "body": "Because of the tricky data arrangement in the sensor.
The first byte is the temperature in °C. The second is 0.5°C in the MSB.
I'm multiplying by 10 to get the temperature in units of 0.1°C and divide by two to get in the 0.5°C units from the low byte.

IMO its easier to have it in °C after the fetch instead of dealing with the 2's complement in the getter function"}

"body": "I'm assuming that the race condition you are considering is in step 5 and 6 below:
1. Start advertising set 0 using identity 0
2. Start advertising set 1 using identity 1
3. Receive LE Connection Complete for advertising set 0
4. Receive LE Connection Complete for advertising set 1
5. Receive LE Advertising Set terminated event for advertising set 0
6. Receive LE Advertising Set terminated event for advertising set 1

column99: the host has no way of mapping the LE Advertising Set Terminated event to the Connection Complete event. That is
column100: it can't map an identity to the newly established connection. \r\n\r\nTherefore
column102: the controller should guarantee that the Advertising Set Terminated event follows the Connection Complete event. Hence

column369: "body": "This whole clock-thing is a bit of a complicated issue.\r\n\r\nIn the Xilinx SoCs
column372: multipliers/dividers etc. relating to the Processor System
column373: integrated peripherals and the programmable logic part have to be configured as part of the FPGA synthesis project in the Vivado IDE (which unfortunately results in redundant work
column374: the whole clock config has to be specified first in Vivado and then in the device tree of the target board
column375: with maybe some defaults at the SoC level of the DT matching the most common configurations). A by-product of the generated FPGA bitstream is an auto-generated C source file which contains loads of register read&write commands which effectively replicate those settings into what eventually becomes the first stage bootloader binary
column376: built by the Xilinx SDK. Therefore
column377: driver for Xilinx peripherals shouldn't mess with any clock configurations during start up
column378: as the system is always pre-configured when booting into the OS.\r\n\r\nThe only exception to that rule are input clock prescalers that can be found for example in the UART for the generation of the configured baud rate
column379: CAN has such a prescaler as well
column381: a prescaler of the input clock is required for the TX clock generation based on the link speed reported by the PHY. The peripheral drivers need not know or actively alter the setting which PLL drives their respective device
column382: they just need to know the actual input frequency
column384: based on which the respective prescaler is calculated
column385: and this value has to be written to the respective peripheral's clock configuration register without modifying any other contents of that register. Therefore
column386: the additional \"clock-frequency\" item in the DT binding is sufficient for the calculation part and is consistent with how input clocks are specified for other device classes such as UARTs etc. As long as there's no \"reg\" property contained in the \"fixed-clock\" class (see explanation below)
column387: I don't think that there's any real benefit in referencing a separate clock node in the DT for the specification of the plain source clock frequency.\r\n\r\nRegarding the clock configuration register to which the prescaler eventually has to be written
column388: there's a bit of an unfortunate design decision by Xilinx: the peripheral clock configuration register are one (Zynq
column393: so that each peripheral's clock configuration register is not contained within the register space specified by each peripheral's \"reg\" property. My initial idea on how to solve this issue was to create one/three clock configuration node(s) in the DT
column394: based on some existing nodes of such type I think I found in the STM32 device trees. This would have allowed to specify (most likely at the board level) the HW oscillator frequency and all the routing / multiplier / divider / clocking scheme informations that configure the entire system's clocks. I added the calculation of frequencies derived from those base settings in the SoC init code
column395: and there was getters for everything at that level
column396: too. Setters were provided for each peripheral's prescaler where required
column397: without the driver having to know its associated register address (this was resolved via the peripheral's base address). The only redundancy (aside from having to set up everything in Vivado first
column398: then having to copy all the data from the synthesis report to the board's DT) then would have been SYS_CLOCK_HW_CYCLES_PER_SEC. The GEM driver in development
column399: and also future implementations such as a CAN
column402: could have just called a getter to obtain the respective input clock frequency
column404: and could have called a setter with the device's base address and the result of the calculation as parameter. That way
column405: no knowledge of bit masking and shifting in the config register (differs slightly between Zynq and UltraScale here and there) would have been required either
column406: one #ifdef less. The moment when all this fell apart was when I realized that even if I shifted the existing UART driver over to this scheme
column407: UART devices always require a \"clock-frequency\" value. At that point
column408: there would have been an inconsistency
column409: so I threw it all out again and opted to make it all consistent again by having the GEM have a \"clock-frequency\" property as well.\r\n\r\nThis still doesn't solve the control register issue
column410: though. The register address could be determined within the driver
column411: but that would require a nested switch first over the current SoC family
column412: then over the current device's base address. Admittedly
column413: that's not a great solution - as the driver currently is
column414: the SoC family switch is already back in for writing to the clock control register due to the slightly different bit positions. So if a \"fixed-clock\" node can have a \"reg\" property without having to introduce an additional (if optional) property that's useless pretty much every other use case
column415: then I'd agree that referencing a separate node that contains both the frequency and the register location would be the best way to solve the issue. But if that is not the case
column416: I'm short on ideas on how to solve the issue elegantly. "}

"body": "@evgeniy-paltsev  @stephanosio  Please note that the `TOOLCHAIN_HAS_NEWLIB` is a CMake variable not accessible in Kconfig.
The reason for the CMake variable can be seen here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/12393
It's intended for the test infrastructure to filter the tests based on the capabilities of the toolchain.

The `SUPPORT_NEWLIB_LIBC` is a Kconfig setting that ensures that a user cannot select `CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC=y` if the toolchain does not support it.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/2b91ebe16e25e5ce17270ea36b88fbb34f5f28ed/lib/libc/Kconfig#L27

column125:
see below feedback from Hardware team at mchp.

1. mec52x and mec172x GPIO logic requires 2 synchronization stages + some extra clocks once an event is detected to clear out the internal logic. This will take ~8 system clock cycles (it can take less).
    we automatically disable clocking for gpio block when there’s no activity and then automatically re-enable clocks when the async detectors capture changes on the pin. This has few clocks delay.
2. It will always trigger an edge detect when turned on if the pin state is the level of the end condition (falling edge = pin state 0; rising edge = pin state 1). It will sometimes trigger an edge detect on any GPIO IRQ configuration change.
3.  dmb instruction has no impact as all ARM AHB accesses stall the processor until completed which gives a large delay between adjacent AHB accesses. 
4. above restriction are applicable only for GPIO block in mec152x device and mec172x device. We need to have delay between write to control register and clearing interrupt status register before enabling GPIO edge detection interrupt.
"}

So to avoid also this race condition we should have the whole init function (or at least the part of it using `shm->instance`) guarded by a spinlock. That is probably not liked by @doki-nordic but I think it is a good enough solution.

Otherwise we should leave the code as is and let the user deal with this kind of problems since he is notified anyway by the error returned by the init function.

https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/guides/device_mgmt/dfu.html#bootloaders
> You need to build and flash MCUboot itself on your device

Zephyr has no dependency to the build of the bootloader in this case.
If I disable the `ExternalProject` code

then Zephyr builds just fine:
```
[140/140] Linking C executable zephyr/zephyr.elf
Memory region         Used Size  Region Size  %age Used

        IDT_LIST:          0 GB         8 KB      0.00%

That is very different from the TF-M case.
The TF-M build produces libraries and object files that is needed by the Zephyr build system in order to link Zephyr itself:
```
arm-zephyr-eabi-gcc
  ...
  -o zephyr/zephyr_prebuilt.elf
  ...
  tfm/platform/libplatform_ns.a  tfm/app/libtfm_api_ns.a  tfm/secure_fw/s_veneers.o
  ...

if I try to disable `TF-M` external project on such build

```

ninja: Entering directory `build'
ninja: error: 'tfm/secure_fw/s_veneers.o'
column667:
missing and no known rule to make it
```

It has been discussed before at TSC that Zephyr should not do multi-image builds in it's CMake build system just for convenience of the user.
Multi image build should be kept outside Zephyr build system.
The reason TF-M is special is because the built output from TF-M is needed for the linking stage of Zephyr itself.

Looking at history I notice that Espressif has been doing this for long time starting here:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/8383

Therefore I think this should be brought up again and discussed at the TSC.
And if approved there
column668: note down under which circumstances the Zephyr build system should allow this approach.\r\n\r\nI'm not against introducing multi-image builds and flashing for the user-convenience

The SETUP stage consists of single transaction:
```
Host->Device | 2d 03 50                         | SETUP Address 3 Endpoint 0 CRC5: 0x0a
Host->Device | c3 00 09 01 00 00 00 00 00 27 25 | DATA0 (0xc3) Actual Request (8 bytes) CRC16 (0x2527)
Device->Host | d2                               | ACK
```

Because wLength was 0
column892:
there is no Data stage and there aren't any transactions on the bus. The state machine directly goes into Status stage.

The Status stage can contain multiple NAKed IN transactions:
```
Host->Device | 69 03 50 | IN Address 3 Endpoint 0 CRC5: 0x0a
Device->Host | 5a       | NAK
```

The Status stage ends with acknowledged IN transaction:
```
Host->Device | 69 03 50 | IN Address 3 Endpoint 0 CRC5: 0x0a
Device->Host | 4b 00 00 | DATA1 (ZLP) CRC: 0x0000
Host->Device | d2       | ACK
```"}

"body": "Lets assume that we would like to use only new logging method using `EVENT_MAANGER_LOG` macro in zephyr. Legacy method is only for backward compatibility in NCS. I would propose following approach: 
- Deprecate legacy logging method (the one less efficient using snprintf)

- Use `_Generic` keyword do detect type of function provided by the user in the macro and assign to one field and leave another as null
- in processing you pick method based on which pointer is not null.

Currently the host supports configuring the controller with long advertising data.

The current implementation sends the data to the controller one AD structure at the time.

And this causes bugs.  If you dig around in kernel/sched.c

column120:
the config name implies only LMA is adjusted.
>
> But the first sentence states that VMA is also adjusted.

That is because the purpose of this flag is to adjust the LMA so that the image may be automatically flashed at a different address or adjusted when converting to hex (bin files are unaffected by this as the don't contain any address information (LMA/VMA)).

When flashing an ELF
column121: the flash tool will use the information provided by LMA to know where to flash the segments.\r\n\r\nBut when using `objcopy --change-addresses` then both LMA and VMA gets adjusted
column122: not only the LMA.\r\nThus I find it important to make the user aware of this
column123: although the purpose is to get LMA adjusted hence the reason for only LMA in the name (we don't care for the VMA in this particular case).\r\n\r\nThere could be other bintools
column124: for example `elfconvert` with the ARM Compiler that supports adjusting only LMA
column125:
but so far I've focused only on GNU bintools.

> And then the second sentence says that the "internal address symbols" are not affected. I assume "interal address symbols" is referring to VMA again. So this contradicts the first sentece.

Internal address symbols are those used by the code and populated by the linker.
For example
column126: if code refers to [__text_region_start](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/5e05393afa5fa8ff291ad91428b8857f8ad47c1c/include/arch/arm/aarch32/cortex_m/scripts/linker.ld#L148) and that symbol points to address `0x00001212`
column127: then the address of that symbol is unaltered when we change LMA. Meaning that if LMA is adjusted with `0x10000000`
column128: then `__text_region_start` is still pointing to `0x00001212`.\r\n\r\nI don't expect all developers to be aware of such details
column129: thus I find it important to inform.\r\n\r\nI will try to see if I can find a better description
column130: but any proposals are more than welcome.\r\nHopefully you get the intention of the sentence now."}

- lpcxpresso54114_m4 and lpcxpresso55s69_cpu0 which uses `generate_inc_file_for_gen_target()` and has a dedicated `SECOND_CORE_MCUX` setting
